solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the name's letters are organised, that is, set out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Andrew has arranged a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' is the anagram signal working on ANDREW.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to roam or stroll aimlessly, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Everyone gets round a Scottish town

parts.note: everyone means all
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Everybody does a lap of a little Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in central Scotland on the River Forth.

definitions.meaning: golf clubs used for the long tee shot
people at the wheel of cars

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the longest golf clubs and people who steer cars.

indicators.note: the leaders of these three words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone reading the Guardian admires its editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like newspaper editorials but asks for first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a slangy, dismissive term for a newspaper of poor quality.

indicators.note: the arrival word comes before the artist in the answer's order

parts.note: arrived means came
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A director turned up ahead of a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera literally makes film footage, a witty take on a director.

clue.text: Singer, one drowned by most of orchestra, unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately awry here are the letters, jumbled into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter

explanation.surface: A vocalist is sadly drowned out by nearly the full orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims ORCHESTRA to ORCHESTR; with I ('drowned by' it) that pool is shuffled by 'unfortunately'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, so a singer.

clue.text: Somewhere to stay in remote land

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A place to lodge out in a far-off country.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel, a place for travellers to spend the night.

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Italian church features in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a novel is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love story, an example of a novel.

parts.note: all-in wrestling is a freestyle form with few rules, popular on British TV
having fun is having a good time

explanation.surface: A spectator describes a style of wrestling as entertaining in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL-IN wrestling is a British name for freestyle professional wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in due course, when the right moment comes.

definitions.meaning: the price of a ticket on a bus or train
the dishes served, as in simple country cooking

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a passenger's ticket price and the meals on offer.

clue.text: Repetitious exercises in gym, initially boring

parts.note: a drill is training by repetition

indicators.note: initially points to the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Endless repeated workouts in the gym are tedious from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull but is the definition in the sense of making a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring a hole and drilling one are the same action.

clue.text: Surrendered, being deprived of vital organ?

definitions.meaning: handed over, as when goods are handed to someone
read as ..., with the liver taken away

explanation.definitionFit: Handing something over is surrendering it; the playful reading has the liver removed.

clue.text: Can largely dispose of Christmas decoration

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to dispose of goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone can mostly throw away the festive trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is the glittering metallic strands hung on Christmas trees.

clue.text: Name of woman — one's lover, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound match

parts.note: one's is I'S and a lover is an adorer

explanation.surface: A man asks whether a woman's name means his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic accent, I'S ADORER matches the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora is a female first name, as for the dancer Isadora Duncan.

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, signalling the letters take a new form

explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample, a little bit offered to try.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes later

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
one who employs something is a user of it

explanation.surface: A person from Liverpool hires staff and backs a modest firm.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scouser is a native of Liverpool, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouser is the informal British name for someone from Liverpool.

definitions.meaning: the Jewish feast commemorating the Exodus

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means overlook; as one it is the Jewish spring feast.

clue.text: Steps taken to produce tomato sauce

definitions.meaning: dance steps, here the Latin dance
a spicy Mexican sauce of chopped tomato

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Latin American dance and a spicy chopped tomato relish.

clue.text: Examination not really putting off odd characters

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth and so on leaves the even letters

explanation.surface: A test that is not quite genuine discourages eccentric people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' looks like strange people but means letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

indicators.note: installed means set in place within another piece

parts.note: a plug is an advert, AD
employees are men, the workforce

explanation.surface: Workers fit a new plug to fix an appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or put right, close to fixing.

clue.text: Ride wave near shore, with some hesitation

parts.note: a roller is a long breaking wave
the coast is the land by the shore
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A surfer catches a wave close to the beach, a little nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollercoaster is a fairground ride on a steep looping track.

indicators.note: the centre here is all of the word but its two ends

explanation.surface: A youth club that has gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Out means no longer in vogue, the opposite of in.

clue.text: Army rejected shabby item of clothing

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: drab means dull and shabby

explanation.surface: The army turned down a scruffy garment.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, like a herald's coat or a tunic worn over a uniform.

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside the other word

parts.note: to traffic is to trade

explanation.surface: A driver held up in a jam fumes angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars but is the verb meaning deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a noun sense of rant.
